cim_eredeti: Is HeyGen Free? Up to 3 Videos a Month, Paid From $24 (2026)
szoveg_eredeti:
Is HeyGen free? Yes, but only for a small amount. HeyGen’s Free plan gives up to 3 videos a month (1 to 3 depending on your region). Each can be up to 1 minute long, exports at 720p, and carries a HeyGen watermark you can’t remove. Paid plans start at $24/month billed yearly ($29 monthly) for Creator with 600 credits, and Pro starts at $41/month billed yearly ($49 monthly).

HeyGen is the best-known AI avatar video tool. You type a script, and a digital presenter (a stock avatar or a clone of you) says it with lip sync, in 175+ languages on paid plans. This guide covers what the free plan includes, what the paid plans cost, how far the credits go, and when another tool is the better fit. All figures come from HeyGen’s own pages, checked on 2026-10-29. We also compare HeyGen with Synthesia, Hedra, D-ID and Krea. Krea is our product. It does not make avatar videos, and we say so below.

Krea runs Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1 and MiniMax H3 on your images and prompts, plus lip sync for portraits.

Every number below comes from a page we opened on 2026-10-29:

We did not run paid quality tests for this post, so it makes no claims about output quality. Where a vendor’s own pages disagree, we say so.

The typical buyer is a business: training teams, marketers and sales teams who need a person on screen without filming one. The pricing page says HeyGen serves “100,000+ businesses.”

HeyGen’s About page says founder Joshua Xu was an engineer at Snap, building features for Snapchat Ads and the AI camera, before he started HeyGen. It lists offices in Los Angeles (12130 Millennium Drive), San Francisco, Palo Alto and Toronto.

HeyGen is mostly paid, but the free plan is a real, usable trial. Here are the individual and team plans as published on 2026-10-29:

What do HeyGen credits buy? HeyGen’s help center publishes per-minute rates. Avatar IV costs 16 credits per minute with a photo avatar and 31 with a video avatar. Avatar V costs 48, Video Agent costs 80 (240 in Seedance mode), and video translation costs 6 per minute with lip sync (10 in Precision mode, 4 without lip sync). How can I use HeyGen for free? Sign up for the Free plan, with no credit card. You get 1 to 3 videos a month depending on your region, each up to 1 minute. Use them to test a stock avatar, a custom avatar, and one translation before you pay. Everything you export is 720p with a watermark.

For avatar video, HeyGen is the category leader, and its pricing is clear. Three things to check before you subscribe:

Synthesia is HeyGen’s most direct competitor: AI avatars, dubbing and templates, aimed at training and internal comms. Its free Basic plan includes “10 minutes of Studio video creation or dubbing” and 500 credits, but “videos carry a Synthesia watermark,” and downloading starts on Starter. Starter is $19/month ($9 for the first month during the current promotion) with 1,250 credits, which Synthesia puts at about 12 minutes of video. Pro is $89/month with 6,000 credits (about 60 minutes). Synthesia exports Full HD at 1920x1080.

Pick it over HeyGen if you produce training content and want its templates, roleplays and surveys (Starter lists 125+ stock avatars). It stops at downloads, which aren’t available on free.

Hedra makes models that animate a character image to an audio track, with more expressive faces than a typical corporate avatar. Its API is prepaid with “no subscription, no seats, no minimum,” from 2.5¢ per second for avatar and lip sync and from 1.13¢ per second for video generation. Studio plans start “from $20/month.” The Studio plan table didn’t load for us, so we can’t list its tiers. Hedra’s lip sync model is also available inside Krea’s lip sync tool.

Pick it if you want a stylized or cartoon character to talk, or you need lip sync through an API. It stops at translation and corporate avatar libraries.

D-ID turns a single photo into a talking head. Its trial is 14 days with 3 minutes and a “full-screen watermark.” Billed yearly, Lite is $4.70/month (10 minutes, watermarked) and Pro is $16/month (15 minutes, commercial use license). We could only load the annual prices.

Pick it if you need a few short talking-photo clips on a small budget. It stops at minutes: 10 to 15 a month on the lower plans.

Krea is our product, so here is the plain version. Krea doesn’t make avatar presenters, doesn’t translate videos, and has no stock avatar library. If that’s the job, use HeyGen or Synthesia.

You can start from text or from an image, with start and end frames on most models. See image to video on Krea and our roundup of the best image to video AI tools. For a speaking face, Krea Lipsync animates a portrait to an audio track with VEED Fabric or Hedra. You can upload audio, record it, or generate speech from text in the same tool. You can upscale finished clips to 4K with the video upscaler, and Krea Agent plans multi-shot sequences from one brief.

Pick Krea over HeyGen if you’re making ads, B-roll, music videos or short films and want to choose the model per shot. It stops at avatars, translation and long talking-head videos.

If you only need a few short generated clips, Google Flow gives everyone 50 credits a day, about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips of up to 8 seconds. It has no avatars or translation.
